points.description: States that the queue is implemented using a circular array, i.e. the array is treated as circular/ring-like rather than as a simple linear array.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer says to use an array with front/rear indices but does not indicate circular or wrap-around use.

levels.says: Says to use an array (possibly with front/rear indices) but does not mention a circular array or treating the array as circular.

points.description: States that the front of the queue is kept toward the beginning of the array and the rear toward the end of the array.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only one of the two placements (front near beginning or rear near end) is stated.

levels.says: Mentions only the front position or only the rear position, not both.

points.description: States that the rear pointer is allowed to wrap around to the beginning of the array when it reaches the end.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if wrap-around is mentioned but not specifically for the rear pointer.

levels.says: Mentions wrap-around/reusing the start of the array but does not say the rear pointer wraps.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the answer to identify a circular array, describe front and rear placement at opposite ends, and say the rear pointer wraps around. Part marks are available for an array-based answer that lacks the circular/wrap-around idea, or for stating only part of the pointer placement or wrap-around detail. No marks are earned for an answer that only says to use an array without any queue pointer or circular-array idea.
